complete_semantic_decision_read.full_chain_observation:
registration and real state producer: Actual @Mod common setup registers ReviveEventServer and all three packets; player AttachCapabilities provides LazyOptional<Bleeding>. HIGHEST LivingDeath on server requires active configuration (creative exception, singleplayer flag or published server) and non-bypass source. A first qualifying death removes the player from helper lists, sends helper-stop, calls knockOut via startBleeding, dismounts if needed, cancels death, adjusts hunger and health. knockOut initializes bleeding/progress/downedTime/timeLeft and saves source/tracker. Already-bleeding death clears current helpers and returns without cancelling; bypass sources skip this entire block. Native Forge listener composition is not verified.
actual damage refusal while downed: LivingHurt first checks bleeding, then lets bypass sources through. Otherwise bledOut, downedTime <= initialDamageCooldown, and independently configured player/mob/other source categories can setCanceled(true). Initial grace is inclusive; flags do not form universal invulnerability. Nonbleeding helper damage optionally removes helper membership. Death/Hurt and active-check conditions differ; hurt listener has no isReviveActive condition. PlayerMixin visibility and optional push refusal read the same state. These generic predicates are support0 under the one cooperative mechanism.
helper admission and membership transfer: Server EntityInteract targeting a bleeding player cancels the interaction. Optional required item checks helper main hand; first consumptive admission shrinks one unless creative, sets inventory changed and target itemConsumed. Once itemConsumed is true, later admissions still enter the else-if ingredient check, but do not shrink again. After these checks, removePlayerAsHelper removes the helper from every current server player list, then adds it to this target and sends HelperPacket(targetUUID,true). The handler itself has no explicit helper-alive/nonbleeding, distance, same-dimension or line-of-sight guard; native interaction pipeline constraints not expanded. Failed item check leaves old membership unchanged. Removal-before-add prevents ordinary repeated interaction from accumulating duplicate entries, not arbitrary API mutations.
competing progress and bleed timer consumer: Server START PlayerTick requires active configuration and alive target, then ticks only bleeding state. Bleeding.tick forces swimming when current pose differs, removes helpers whose numeric distance is >maxDistance and sends stop to those helpers. It does not separately check level identity, alive, current held item, sustained button hold or current bleeding state. If no helpers OR haltBleedTime=false, decrement timeLeft; if none AND resetProgress=true, zero progress. Then add remaining helper count * progressPerPlayer, increment downedTime, and request configured helper food exhaustion. Parent sends snapshots every five downed ticks and applies configured effects/hunger before checking revived progress first, then bledOut. If both predicates true that tick, revive wins. Effects admission results ignored; progress does not depend on hunger payment success.
authoritative release and terminal path: revive clears Bleeding state first, requests configured effects, resetPlayer sends stop to current helpers and clears list/PersistentData flag, syncs, writes healthAfter, requests revived sound, posts PlayerRevivedEvent, syncs again, releases forced pose. Event comment says before revived but actual call follows state/health writes. kill posts PlayerBleedOutEvent (not used as a returned veto), restores original combat snapshot, writes HP0, forceBledOut, calls die(saved/fallback source), clears helpers/flag with an intermediate snapshot, then clears Bleeding state and forced pose and sends final snapshot. Marking bleeding/time0 before die prevents its own first-death rescue branch from rearming. The native die result/cross-mod cancellation is not certified; reset occurs even if native death is intercepted. Logout bleeding calls kill; permission2 command directly revives bleeding targets. Optional upstream ban policy is read as context only and is never proposed for Dynasty.
actual consumer and acknowledgement boundary: ReviveUpdatePacket snapshots target UUID and serialized timeLeft/progress/bleeding/consumed. Client execution looks up that UUID in current Minecraft level, drops absent target, deserializes into capability and forces STANDING if false. HelperPacket independently writes static helpActive/helpTarget. Registered RenderGuiOverlayEvent.Post consumer shows helper target time/progress if helper is not bleeding, helpActive, GUI visible, no screen and target UUID resolves. It does not test target.isBleeding or actual helper membership. Victim overlay reads own state, applies pose/handsBusy/missTime and local jump effect; on nonbleeding overlay it restores post effect, clears jump/handsBusy and explicitly stops owned sound. Low-level CreativeCore delivery, native graphics/shader/audio engine internals are not expanded; no visual/audio success claim.
incomplete notification coverage is an observed chain property: removePlayerAsHelper only removes from server lists and sends no HelperPacket. Damage abort calls only that helper. Therefore under abortOnDamage=true, a removed helper can retain helpActive=true and a resolved old target overlay: later target reset iterates remaining helpers, so it does not notify the removed one. Distance pruning does send stop; switching targets sends a new start; first knockOut of the helper sends stop; target normal revive/kill sends stop to helpers still present. A bypass-source death skips the playerDied helper cleanup, and already-bleeding non-bypass death only clears helpers there, not all bleeding state. These are static branch observations, not runtime reproduced defects. No claim every death/logout/dimension change is covered.
give-up and client lifecycle boundaries: Client END tick increments a local hold counter while bleeding and attack held; sends GiveUpPacket only when prior counter > seconds*20 then resets it. Server checks only sender bleeding before kill, not hold duration. Render callback has no per-overlay-type filter here, so do not infer one call per frame. Helper static fields have no disconnect/session reset in the complete local Java files; target lookup includes current world but packet carries no dimension/session/sequence and no queue. If player is null, render cleanup does not run; absence of a drawn target is not clearing helpActive. Audio TensionSound tick is empty, so owned sound stop must not be inferred from that wrapper alone. These are support limits, not extra UI/transport credits.

Generic first-death cancellation, self-countdown DBNO, source category refusal, packets, numeric constants, defects and UI are all support0. This is not a second generic DBNO or a new presentation family.

whole_chain_observation: Concrete registration: RegistryRecipeTypes.init calls AttunementCraftingRegistry.init from prior primer startup, registering AttunePlayerRecipe plus crystal recipe in a HashMap. Altar first matching values iteration has no sorted priority guarantee. Registered BlockAttunementAltar creates actual TileAttunementAltar, and tile registry builds its reflected factory. CommonProxy registers invulnerability listeners and SERVER timeout; ClientProxy registers camera manager with Observer tick and camera render listener. Native block placement/Observer structure engine/runtime registry success unexecuted; no building design credit.

Admission requires cached sky visibility and observed multiblock, active constellation search and night. Altar sky checks are cached up to20ticks; constellation scan every20. Recipe requires IMajor active constellation and chooses closest ServerPlayer in unit box at altar.up grown1 BEFORE eligibility, so an ineligible closest player prevents trying another candidate. Eligibility is alive/nonfake/nonsneaking, valid progress, unattuned, tier>=ATTUNEMENT and discovered current constellation. Fake helper rejects Forge FakePlayer/unapproved subclass/missing connection/address errors; external Mods class lookup unexpanded. No ingredient/payment exists in this player recipe.

createRecipe repeats closest lookup, captures that player UUID and current major constellation; start positions that player at altar offset twice. Active.matches first reruns recipe.canStartCrafting (some closest eligible player), then separately requires captured UUID player present/alive in altar world; it does not require these two player identities equal or captured constellation equal current altar constellation. Server tick calls active.tick (grant then increments age) BEFORE matches, so an invalidated current recipe can grant one last pass. Sky/multiblock early failure instead nulls recipe before grant; neither invalidation branch calls stopCrafting. stopCrafting itself is empty for this recipe.

Every server doTick with captured player present invokes EventHelperInvulnerability.makeInvulnerable: unconditionally setInvulnerable(true), append a new timeout10 entry containing PlayerEntity object. TimeoutList.add does not deduplicate or renew. contains compares value.equals across entries. A repeated grant is not a source-owned lease/refcount or one refreshed deadline. No snapshot of prior invulnerable flag is saved; no UUID/dimension/generation metadata is stored in this helper. Only this active-player recipe is a native producer in the fixed Java call-site scan.

Three effective protection paths differ. Native invulnerable flag is set at grant; LOW LivingHurt cancels any player with list membership without local amount/source/bypass/side predicate; LivingSetAttackTarget requires live player target and membership, then clears revenge target and Mob attack target. It changes targeting, not every AI memory or all direct control. No success-specific packet, gray text, sound or result is produced by these hooks; exact Forge/native damage/target recursion and other listeners remain external.

SERVER END timeout decrements each entry and unconditionally calls player.setInvulnerable(false) before removing each expired entry. It does not inspect remaining entries. Thus older expiries can clear native flag while newer membership still cancels Hurt/target assignment; relative tile/END order is not a runtime guarantee. Stopping recipe stops new grants but existing entries retain residue until their remaining dispatched ticks expire. Ordinary recipe completion/stopEffects does not immediately clear list or flag. Never infer complete invulnerability from camera presence or from one of these states alone.

Logout removes ALL equal player entries through removeIf without the expiry delegate, so this handler does not restore/clear the native flag. Server cache cleanup invokes clearServer, whose TimeoutList.clear calls delegate for every remaining entry then clears. No prior-flag restoration in either path, and duplicate clears are possible. Clone/dimension transfer/object replacement/native entity destruction are not modeled here: list keys are retained player objects, not UUIDs, and no survival across real process restart is claimed.

Authoritative default finish: Active age>=800 after server tick and matches permits Tile.finishActiveRecipe. It invokes recipe.finishRecipe then empty stopCrafting, nulls currentRecipe, marks block update and submits two ambient flares. finishRecipe calls ResearchManager.setAttunedConstellation using CAPTURED constellation. Setter rejects invalid progress/undiscovered constellation, otherwise removes allocated perks, zeroes experience, sets attuned state, optionally applies root, requests advancement, progress sync and save; it returns bool. Active ignores that bool, so tile teardown/flares are not proof progression settled. Existing migration owner owns persistence/research; this is API-boundary support0 and no transaction/disk success claim.

Tile synchronization uses writeNetNBT for current constellation and recipe key/tick/playerUUID/captured constellation; getUpdatePacket includes it. Chunk write and getUpdateTag omit writeNetNBT, so this class does not persist active ceremony or include it in normal initial tag. readNetNBT replaces same recipe instance via deserialize while reusing previous cameraHack only; startedPlayerSound resets with new instance. Invalid/missing recipe calls previous stopEffects then nulls. External native update delivery, chunk bootstrap and rendering are unexecuted; no continuous timer sync or resume-across-save guarantee.

Local camera starts only for matching UUID. Builder creates400 path points*2ticks and player-focus transformer, placed in priority-only TreeSet; equal priority can reject another transformer without a result checked by caller. Render START chooses highest, starts/stops on changes, renders and removes expired; CLIENT START while unpaused advances camera age. CameraPath expires when ticksExisted>total800, unlike server recipe>=800. No shared authoritative clock. Tick delegate locks REPLACEMENT position/orientation, hides its custom name and zeroes velocity; rendering helper also writes actual local player pose/position to camera location. EntityCameraRenderView ignores rotation input; no full server control/input-ban assertion.

Camera settings snapshot GUI/view-bobbing/viewpoint/flying and start pose, sets GUI hidden/third-person/flying during rendering. PlayerFocus creates a local replacement from player NBT; stop restores cached settings/pose first, then overwrites actual local pose with replacement final pose, removes replacement, resets render camera and may close current screen, and invokes path stop delegate if world nonnull. Thus return is not simply original pose. These are source reads only: no actual UI/focus/sound/brightness/game action performed.
